C5.exact_target: F2 times F2 cannot be written as a nontrivial amalgam over Z.
assumptions_and_scope: F2 is free of rank2 in each of the two direct factors.
Nontrivial amalgam means the genuine splitting with proper edge inclusions; its Bass-Serre action is simplicial and without inversions.
The selected edge group is infinite cyclic. No HNN, arbitrary small-edge, or general product no-splitting theorem is asserted.
mature_inputs_used: Bass-Serre tree for an amalgam and its vertex/edge stabilizers
A hyperbolic tree isometry has a unique invariant axis; commuting isometries preserve it
On an oriented simplicial axis, orientation-preserving isometries have additive integer displacement; an isometry commuting with a nonzero translation cannot reverse the axis
Nonzero powers of two distinct free generators freely generate a rank2 free subgroup; cyclic groups do not contain such a subgroup
actual_author_core: Find a hyperbolic product element a=(g,h) and use both commuting factor elements to preserve its unique axis.
Select a nontrivial axis translation in one factor and force both generators of the other factor to preserve the same axis.
Use the two displayed mixed elements x^k*c1^(-n) and x^m*d1^(-n) in the pointwise-axis kernel; their other-factor projections retain independent nonzero powers of c and d.
Put this rank2 free subgroup in an edge stabilizer, contradicting the cyclic edge group.

translation_parameter_decision.source_words: If n,k,m are the translation lengths of x,c1,d1 respectively
translation_parameter_decision.necessary_reading: Use the integer signed displacements of those three restrictions to the same oriented axis; n is nonzero, while k,m may be zero or negative.
translation_parameter_decision.why_ordinary: The author already writes the two cancellation elements. A common oriented-axis coordinate is ordinary bookkeeping for those translations and adds no group hypothesis or new kernel construction. The proof does not require c1 or d1 individually hyperbolic.
translation_parameter_decision.literal_unsigned_limit: If translation length is reserved for its usual nonnegative metric meaning, the sentence is imprecise: absolute lengths alone do not force the displayed cancellation when directions differ. Preserve that caveat. Do not claim the unsigned formula is literally valid without a direction convention.
translation_parameter_decision.treatment: Disclose signed-displacement interpretation in metadata; retain the original PDF and exponents unchanged.

C6_context.claim: For a chosen vertex group Gv, quotient by the normal closure of all incident edge-group images is an epimorphic image of the graph-of-groups fundamental group.
C6_context.actual_author_argument: The source projects Gv and kills all other presentation generators; the graph-of-groups relators vanish by the specified normal closure.
C6_context.role: H1 author context for C7, not an extra selected target.

C7.exact_target: Every finitely generated subgroup H of the printed cyclic double Fn*_<c>Fn is finitely presented.
assumptions_and_scope: Fn has the printed finite rank n; H is finitely generated.
Subgroup vertex stabilizers are subgroups of conjugates of Fn, hence free by Nielsen-Schreier; they are not assumed finitely generated initially.
Subgroup edge stabilizers are cyclic, including possible trivial groups. No maximal-cyclic, primitive-c, or non-proper-power hypothesis is inserted.
Only the printed cyclic double is selected; not an arbitrary coherent-amalgam theorem.
mature_inputs_used: Nielsen-Schreier: subgroups of a free group are free
Chosen-transversal S-normal-form uniqueness and reduction, compatible on a subgraph
Every finite collection of elements of a free group is supported by finitely many elements of any fixed free basis
A quotient of a finitely generated group is finitely generated; an infinite-rank free group is not
Finite graph-of-groups presentations with finitely presented vertex groups and finitely generated edge groups are finite presentations

finite_core_boundary.actual_author_step: Choose finite Y containing the paths in words for a finite generating set, then use S-normal forms to identify H=pi1(A,Y,a0).
finite_core_boundary.check: Take the finite union of based generator paths (and the common basepoint). Products and reduction of these words introduce no new underlying edges outside that union. The chosen normal-form statement and subgraph injection identify the resulting subgroup with the finite graph-of-groups group.
finite_core_boundary.source_precision: The phrase unique reduced path must be read as uniqueness under fixed S representatives/normal-form convention. Arbitrary reduced graph-of-groups spellings are not unique. This is a routine convention, not an extra coherence theorem.

compressed_infinite_rank_bridge.source_sentence: By the previous exercise if a vertex group is not finitely generated we have an epimorphism from H to a free group of infinite rank.
conditions_actually_available: Y is finite, so a fixed vertex has finitely many incident oriented edges in the selected core.
Each edge group is cyclic; their images are normally generated by finitely many vertex-group words.
If the free vertex group had infinite rank, finitely many words involve only a finite subset of its free basis.

The elementary free-group quotient obtained by killing that finite basis subset remains free of infinite rank and kills the incident words, so the C6 quotient has the required further epimorphic image.
compressed_infinite_rank_bridge.key_distinction: It is not necessary, and not generally true, that Gv/N itself is a free group. C6 followed by the elementary free quotient gives an epimorphism from H to an infinite-rank free group.
compressed_infinite_rank_bridge.judgment: This is an ordinary finite-support/universal-property consequence of the mature free-group inputs. It is a compressed condition check, not a missing new lemma or a new source-specific construction. No target theorem is being treated as a prior.
compressed_infinite_rank_bridge.preservation: The review records this standard-input boundary; it does not append a replacement author proof or modify the source pages.

C7.finite_presentation_end: With finite Y and all vertex groups now finitely generated free, they are finitely presented. Cyclic edge groups have finite generating sets, so the standard finite graph-of-groups presentation (or finitely many amalgam/HNN steps) applies. The author states this final assembly explicitly.
C7.H2_threshold: The author derives two necessary finiteness conclusions from the finite generation of H: a finite underlying graph core via normal forms, and finite generation of every inherited free vertex group via C6 and a free quotient obstruction. These are then assembled into the finite presentation. None of the listed priors supplies the target coherence result. The linked global-to-local finiteness argument supports lower-end H2; there is no H3 evidence.
